questions.q: Buses are scheduled to arrive at a stop every 10 minutes on average, but in practice the gaps between buses vary — some longer, some shorter. A passenger who arrives at a uniformly random time will, on average, wait:
choices: Longer than 5 minutes, because of the inspection (waiting-time) paradox
Exactly 5 minutes, since that is half the average gap
It depends only on the bus schedule and is never more than 5 minutes
Less than 5 minutes, since most gaps are short
